title: Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini: Best AI for Your First Website? Go Live Free, No Coding
description:
You don't code, but you want to build your own one-page website by chatting: how Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini differ, and which one a free account can actually use.
For anyone who wants a personal site or portfolio but doesn't want to learn HTML first.

This video runs the same brief through all three and compares their entrances, plans and limits. Then it shows step by step how to change one thing at a time, put the site online for free with GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, and search for your own phone number, address and keys before you publish. Plans and limits follow the official sites on the day; checked on September 30, 2026.

chapters.five-parts: How to write a website prompt
chapters.get-file: How to edit an AI-made website
chapters.answer: Best AI for your first website

6jm7.text: All three AIs build websites by chat, but your free account may not get all of them.

9acq.text: This video tests all three on one brief, then gets you live for free.

32bz.text: You think picking a tool means finding the stronger model.

yck8.text: The real first gate: can your account use it?

hsiq.text: So what do the three official pages say?

z52a.text: Claude's is Artifacts; free plans can create them in chat.

3rhn.text: Gemini's is Canvas; officially, every Gemini user can use it.

swky.text: ChatGPT's is Sites; officially, Free and Go plans don't have it.

aini.text: All three look alike; the difference is your account.

sbwf.text: Officially stated to work on free plans: Claude and Gemini.

7up6.text: ChatGPT states that Free and Go plans don't have it.

x9sq.text: To try all three on one brief, how should you write that brief?

tm5t.text: Start with purpose: who the page is for and what they do next.

q87a.text: Then content: paste in the words yourself.

9unv.text: Be specific on style: off-white, dark green accents.

u297.text: Fourth is often skipped: what to leave out.

2b4k.text: Last, add technical limits on the file's shape.

hti7.text: Without saying what you don't want, AI adds lots you don't need.

s5hs.text: First, this one: "Make me a website" leaves AI guessing.

t4ni.text: This one covers all four, so it comes closer to what you want.

pjat.text: My view: not coding isn't the barrier. Stating needs clearly is.

dv87.text: Tell it you want just one HTML file, named index.html.

ztfe.text: Put the styles in that same file.

wm55.text: No external images or fonts, and no framework.

frv7.text: Paste it in all three, swapping the brackets for your own.

ctf9.text: The brief is ready; where is each of the three entrances?

iret.text: Claude is most direct: paste the brief and it opens beside the chat.

tyw4.text: Gemini: pick Canvas below the text box, then paste the brief.

8jfe.text: On ChatGPT web, pick Work first.

xvtz.text: Write "website" in the prompt, or mention Sites.

wpkd.text: Check that the Code execution and file creation switch is on.

j3xg.text: Officially, Artifacts need it, and free plans have it on by default.

39ct.text: Claude's plus: free plans can create them; check one setting.

yrac.text: Gemini lets you edit code; on a preview error, open the console.

6x9c.text: But official help lists no web-file download under export.

i6k9.text: ChatGPT does everything from description to publishing in one place, but it's in public beta.

e4kn.text: ChatGPT's official FAQ is very direct about it.

epsd.text: Sites is not available on the Free plan or the Go plan.

uyi5.text: Simple: open a new chat in each and paste the same brief.

3aaf.text: Save each result in its own folder, every file named index.html.

djbb.text: Open them side by side; skip the one your account can't use.

wskr.text: You can see by eye which comes closer.

fvv9.text: Names and plans change fast; go by the official site that day.

p2zu.text: You have a tool and the file; how do you edit without making a mess?

x9y8.text: Make it a file: download if there's a button, else copy all the code.

y8wd.text: Paste it into a plain text editor, save as index.html, in a new folder.

cbym.text: Double-click, open in a browser: what others really see.

fi98.text: Buttons move; if you can't find one, copy.

9e6i.text: A fine preview panel doesn't mean the file itself is fine.

4hsz.text: Read the text through, then click every link to check they go right.

zhva.text: Last, narrow the window; is the phone layout cramped?

izrh.text: This check is about the look and text, not the code.

g5pn.text: Template and three edit prompts are in the article.

39fm.text: The article link is the first line of the description.

dftp.text: Copy the template as is; replace the brackets with your content.

2zbn.text: Don't send five requests at once.

nieh.text: First, change only colors; say which part and what color.

6ijm.text: Second, add one section; say where it goes.

sxwe.text: Third, fix mobile; describe the narrow layout.

fgdh.text: Too much at once: fixes often break others.

98ag.text: Third is the mobile prompt: name the scope and result.

4tvp.text: Last line: make it say which breakpoint it used, so you know if anything else changed.

i69p.text: Say make the title dark green and the work area two columns, and it knows what to do.

3r7m.text: After each round, download again and reopen it to look.

tjmt.text: After some rounds, midway versions slip online.

qfg7.text: So save a backup each time you're happy.

yqcj.text: Backed up; how do you put this version online for free?

a4vh.text: Put the file on a free static site host.

hvjf.text: GitHub Pages: sites up to 1 GB, and a soft monthly bandwidth limit of 100 GB.

bguq.text: Cloudflare Pages allows 500 builds a month and up to 20,000 files per site.

knvi.text: Tell soft and hard limits apart.

wyvs.text: A GitHub site, for example, can't go over 1 GB.

4raw.text: GitHub Pages has a soft limit of 10 builds per hour.

svsx.text: Building and publishing with a custom GitHub Actions workflow is not subject to this limit.

sitm.text: Before going live, tidy the folder to the basics.

5ymd.text: Name this one-page HTML file index.html, so once uploaded it serves as the site's entry.

5y3q.text: Put images in the same folder; lowercase English names, no spaces.

z4ax.text: Inconsistent names or paths may stop the live page from opening.

7g2d.text: In Cloudflare, create a direct-upload project to drag in the folder.

25nv.text: One drag-and-drop holds up to 1,000 files.

ihai.text: GitHub's rule: Pages can't be a free host for an online business or store.

5azv.text: Personal pages and portfolios are fine; to sell, use another service.

7f5w.text: On GitHub's free plan, Pages only works from a public repository.

vy3f.text: Anyone can see what you put up.

wvvw.text: What I do: before going live, I open index.html in a plain text editor.

kuii.text: Search for your phone and address.

2gnu.text: Then search for your ID number.

d4hc.text: Also search once for any string that looks like a key.

ykf6.text: Check this step yourself, carefully; don't just trust AI saying the file is fine.

e4d8.text: Page source is public; deleted text may stay in others' caches.

m8xm.text: It's live; which of the three actually suits you?

k26g.text: Free account only? Officially, Claude and Gemini work.

sbpk.text: Already on Gemini? Try Canvas first; check plan limits on the official site.

6yd4.text: With Plus, Pro or a workspace, you can try ChatGPT Sites too.

tie9.text: Back to the start: whether your account works decides it.

s5cf.text: The rest is the same method: full brief, one change at a time, search for personal data before going live.

cuqe.text: So pick the one you can use, then follow the article in the description to make your first page.
